If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67) and recent price is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid overestimating continuation.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and price is trending up, add a 2–3% downward bias to late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect reversal risk.

If sentiment is positive but recent price is falling, apply a 1–2% upward correction to early horizon to counteract sentiment-driven overconfidence.

If sentiment is negative and price is falling, maintain forecast unchanged for mid horizon unless sentiment turns positive within 3 days, then trigger a 1.5% upward adjustment.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing adjustment across all horizons to reduce overfitting to short-term noise.
